question: Should the experimental Claw ownership ledger and its Doctor diagnostics be accepted as a core OpenClaw feature, rather than remaining an unlanded stacked implementation or moving to an extension-oriented design?
rationale: The patch is technically scoped as experimental, but it creates a durable core CLI/Doctor/state ownership model whose placement and staged landing order cannot be resolved from code review alone.

options.title: Sponsor the core stack
options.body: Accept the lifecycle ownership model as a core direction, review and land the prerequisite ownership slice first, then require this rebased PR’s current-head proof before merge.

options.title: Keep diagnostics outside core
options.body: Decline the core Doctor/ownership direction and ask for a plugin or external workflow only if existing public seams can provide the needed lifecycle data.

options.title: Pause pending RFC decision
options.body: Leave the stack open but do not merge its slices until the linked RFC has a maintainer-backed scope decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core stack
recommendation.body: Accept the lifecycle ownership model as a core direction, review and land the prerequisite ownership slice first, then require this rebased PR’s current-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This reviewer supplied the most concrete recorded requirements for the diagnostic’s operational and read-only contracts.
